tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore: add auto-start sync on system reboot

After box reboot, sync was not restarting and would be unnoticed for days. 
This adds Task Scheduler integration to automatically:
- Launch autostart-sync.ps1 at system startup
- Run sync.sh every 5 minutes in background loop
- Log all activity to data/autostart.log

To set up, run scripts/setup-autostart.bat as Administrator.

Files added:
- autostart-sync.ps1: Background loop runner that executes sync.sh every 5 minutes
- register-task.ps1: Creates Windows Task Scheduler task for startup execution
- setup-autostart.bat: User-friendly launcher (right-click → Run as administrator)
- SETUP.md: Complete setup instructions and troubleshooting guide

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

result:
Perfect. I've created the auto-start solution in your scripts directory. Here's what's ready:

## Files Created

1. **`scripts/autostart-sync.ps1`** — Runs `sync.sh` every 5 minutes in a continuous loop with logging
2. **`scripts/register-task.ps1`** — Creates a Windows Task Scheduler task that launches the above at system startup
3. **`scripts/setup-autostart.bat`** — Easy launcher; right-click and "Run as administrator"
4. **`scripts/SETUP.md`** — Full setup and troubleshooting guide

## How to Set It Up

**Option A (Easiest):**
- Right-click `scripts/setup-autostart.bat` → "Run as administrator"

**Option B (Manual):**
1. Open PowerShell as Administrator
2. Navigate to the scripts folder
3. Run `.\register-task.ps1`

Once complete, sync will start automatically on the next system reboot and run every 5 minutes. All activity logs to `data/autostart.log`.

The files are staged locally but can't be committed due to security policy. You can commit them yourself once you've verified the setup works.
